mainTopic: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reliance on רבי שמעון, the materials and surfaces for writing a גט, and how witnesses who cannot sign may sign a גט
overview: The amud opens as רבי יהושע בן לוי finishes his ruling: in a pressing situation, we may rely on רבי שמעון, who allows a גט written by day and signed later. The גמרא checks this against ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן, and concludes that he follows רבי יוחנן on timing and ריש לקיש on the role of the extra signers. A new משנה then teaches that a גט may be written with any lasting ink, on almost any surface, even a cow's horn or a slave's hand, as long as the wife receives that object; רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids living things and food. The גמרא defines the inks and adds more lasting materials from ברייתות of רבי חנינא and רבי חייא. It brings a related שבת law about tracing one ink over another, which can count as both writing and erasing. ריש לקיש then asks whether witnesses who cannot sign may trace over names written for them in red dye, and רבי יוחנן says that kind of tracing is not real writing for a גט. The אמוראים offer other methods where the first marking does not count as writing: a paper stencil, plain lead, gall water on treated parchment, and saliva. Finally, the גמרא limits this help to גיטין only, and a story shows that רב כהנא had a man flogged for using it on ordinary documents.

steps.title: Relying on רבי שמעון in a pressing situation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that one may rely on רבי שמעון's lenient view in a time of need.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון is worthy of being relied upon in a pressing situation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי finishes his ruling. In a case where the signing of the גט was delayed, we may lean on רבי שמעון's lenient view, but only when there is real need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows a גט written during the day and signed at night, even though the date no longer matches the signing. רבי יהושע בן לוי does not follow this view in general. He uses it as a backup only in a time of pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: in a pressing or urgent situation

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole back-and-forth that follows. The גמרא now checks whether relying on רבי שמעון here fits with the views of ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon is worthy
to be relied upon in a pressing situation.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדַאי הוּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לִסְמוֹךְ עָלָיו בִּשְׁעַת הַדְּחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a pressing situation, one may rely on רבי שמעון's lenient view about a גט signed after the time it was written.

steps.title: ריש לקיש limits רבי שמעון to immediate signing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling using ריש לקיש, who says רבי שמעון only allowed signing right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't ריש לקיש say that רבי שמעון only allowed it when signed immediately, but not if signed any time from now up to ten days later?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יהושע בן לוי. According to ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון's leniency does not cover a delayed signing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case, the other signers might sign days later. If ריש לקיש is right, רבי שמעון would not allow such a גט either. So relying on רבי שמעון would not help.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't Reish Lakish say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֶלָּא לְאַלְתַּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon validated it only if signed immediately,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִכָּאן וְעַד עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים – לָא!
phrases.english: but from now until ten days later, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reliance on רבי שמעון for a delayed signing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון only allows immediate signing, so his view cannot support a signing that is delayed.

steps.title: On timing, he follows רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that on the question of timing, רבי יהושע בן לוי holds like רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that point, he holds like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע בן לוי simply does not accept ריש לקיש's limit. On this issue he sides with רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן is understood to disagree with ריש לקיש here. He holds that רבי שמעון allows the signing even after a delay. So relying on רבי שמעון still works for our case.

keyTerms.meaning: in that matter / on that point

phrases.english: On that point, he holds like Rabbi Yochanan.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע בן לוי, and 'that point' is whether a delayed signing is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing a side in a dispute: the ruling follows the other Amora on this point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי שמעון's leniency is limited to immediate signing, as ריש לקיש says.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע בן לוי follows רבי יוחנן, so a delayed signing is still covered by רבי שמעון.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן says the extra signers are not real witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: according to רבי יוחנן, only two signers are עדים, and the rest sign only because of the husband's condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: two sign as עדים, and all the rest sign only because of the condition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If רבי יהושע בן לוי follows רבי יוחנן, there should be no need to lean on רבי שמעון at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the first two signers are the real עדים, and the others sign only to fulfill the husband's request. Then the late signers do not affect whether the גט is valid. So why would רבי יהושע בן לוי need a 'pressing situation' leniency?

keyTerms.meaning: because of the condition (the husband's request)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two disputes. Step 2 was about timing (immediate or delayed). This step is about why the extra people sign: as real עדים, or just because of the condition.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
two sign as witnesses,
and all the rest because of the condition!
phrases.notes: The 'condition' is the husband's instruction that all of them should sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהושע בן לוי follows רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he followed רבי יוחנן, the extra signers would not be real עדים. The גט would be valid without needing רבי שמעון's leniency, yet רבי יהושע בן לוי does rely on it.

steps.title: On the role of the signers, he follows ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that on this point רבי יהושע בן לוי holds like ריש לקיש, that all the signers count as עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: On this point, he holds like ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. רבי יהושע בן לוי follows a different authority on each question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On why everyone signs, he follows ריש לקיש: all the signers are real עדים. That is why a late signature creates a problem and he needs רבי שמעון. On timing, he follows רבי יוחנן, so even a delayed signing is covered.

keyTerms.meaning: in this matter / on this point

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי combines both views. He agrees with ריש לקיש that all the signers are עדים, and with רבי יוחנן that רבי שמעון allows a delayed signing. So, in a pressing situation, he validates the גט by relying on רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: On this point, he holds like Reish Lakish.
phrases.notes: Now the point is why all of them sign. Like ריש לקיש, he holds they all count as real witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the issues: a different authority is followed on each question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי יוחנן on one point meant following him on every point.
steps.terutzMaskana: He follows ריש לקיש on the role of the signers and רבי יוחנן on timing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling fits by taking each point from a different authority.

steps.title: A גט may be written with any lasting material
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a גט may be written with any type of lasting ink or dye.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may write a גט with anything: ink, paint, red dye, tree gum, shoemakers' black dye, or anything that lasts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: what you may write a גט with. It lists several inks and dyes, then gives the general rule that anything lasting is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listed items are only examples. The real test is whether the writing will last. Any material that leaves permanent writing is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: a black dye used by shoemakers (iron sulfate)

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may write with anything:
with ink, with paint, with red dye,
and with tree gum, and with kankantom (a black dye),
and with anything that is lasting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט may be written with any material that produces permanent writing.

steps.title: Not with liquids or anything that fades
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that a גט may not be written with liquids, fruit juice, or anything that does not last.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not write with liquids, nor with fruit juice, nor with anything that does not last.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the rule. Writing that fades is not acceptable for a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids and fruit juices leave marks that disappear. Because the writing will not last, it cannot be used. This matches the test from the first half: a גט needs permanent writing.
steps.whatToRemember: The test for writing a גט is permanence. Lasting ink or dye is fine; anything that fades is not.

phrases.english: One may not write with liquids,
nor with fruit juice,
nor with anything that does not last.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה with the forbidden materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט may not be written with liquids, fruit juice, or any material whose writing does not last.

steps.title: A גט may be written on any surface
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a גט may be written on anything, even an olive leaf, a cow's horn, or a slave's hand, as long as the husband gives her the cow or the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may write a גט on anything: on an olive leaf, or on a cow's horn (and then he gives her the whole cow), or on a slave's hand (and then he gives her the slave).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from what you write *with* (ink) to what you write *on* (the surface). It says almost any surface is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a living animal or person can carry the writing. The catch is that the wife must actually receive the גט. So if it is written on a cow's horn or a slave's hand, the husband hands over the whole cow or the whole slave.

keyTerms.meaning: And he gives her (the object the גט is written on)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the husband is giving the cow as a gift or payment. He gives the cow only because the גט is written on it, and the wife has to receive the גט.

phrases.english: On anything one may write (a גט):
on an olive leaf;
and on the horn of a cow,
and he gives her the cow;
on the hand of a slave,
and he gives her the slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה: after listing the inks, it now lists the surfaces.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט may be written on any surface, including a living animal or slave, as long as the object itself is given to the wife.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids living things and food
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees: a גט may not be written on anything alive or on food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: you may not write a גט on anything that has life in it, and not on food.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה argues with the first one about the cow and slave cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allowed even a cow or a slave. רבי יוסי הגלילי rules out two whole groups: anything living, and food. The משנה gives no reason here, it only states his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Life (literally, 'spirit of life'), meaning a living creature

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion in the משנה: any surface is fine. רבי יוסי הגלילי: not on living things and not on food.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
One may not write, neither on a thing
that has the breath of life in it,
nor on foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the first opinion of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a גט may not be written on a living creature or on food.

steps.title: The גמרא explains the ink names in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the everyday Aramaic names for the inks and dyes the משנה listed: דיו, סם, סיקרא, קומוס, and קנקנתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: דיו is what we call דיותא (ink). סם is סמא. About סיקרא, רבה בר בר חנה said its name is סקרתא (red dye). קומוס is קומא (tree sap). About קנקנתום, רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of שמואל: it is the black stuff that shoemakers use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining words. It translates each ink from the משנה's list into a familiar name so we know what material is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is being argued here. The גמרא is just defining terms, matching each Hebrew word in the משנה to the name people knew in Aramaic. For two of the words it names who gave the explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
A black dye used by shoemakers (iron sulfate)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Deyo is deyota (ink).
Sam is samma (arsenic).

phrases.aramaic: סִיקְרָא – אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: Sikra: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
Its name is sikreta (red dye).
Komos is kuma (tree sap).

phrases.aramaic: קַנְקַנְתּוֹם – אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Kankantom: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Shmuel said:
It is the black (dye) of shoemakers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by going back to the ink list from the משנה (step 6).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each ink in the משנה is matched to a known material: ink, arsenic, red dye, tree sap, and shoemakers' black dye.

steps.title: What does 'anything that lasts' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'and with anything that lasts' and asks what extra case it comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'and with anything that lasts.' What does that come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It points to a general phrase in the משנה and asks what new case it adds beyond the inks already listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already named five specific inks. If it then adds 'anything that lasts,' it must mean to include something more. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: To include what? (what does this phrase add?)
Etc. The rest of the quote from the משנה is left out

phrases.english: 'And with anything that lasts,' etc.:
To include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the named inks to the general phrase that follows them in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which writing material, not named in the list, is included by 'anything that lasts'?

steps.title: It includes רבי חנינא's case of gallnut water
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the phrase includes רבי חנינא's teaching that a גט written with מי טריא or gallnut water is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include what רבי חנינא taught: if he wrote it with מי טריא or with gallnut water, the גט is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step. It names a ברייתא that lists liquids which still leave lasting writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said liquids and fruit juices are not allowed because they don't last. Here we learn that some liquids, like gallnut water, do leave lasting marks, so they are valid. That is the extra case 'anything that lasts' adds.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of liquid that leaves a lasting mark

steps.confusionAlert: This does not argue with the משנה's rule against liquids. That rule was about liquids that don't last. These liquids do last.

phrases.english: To include that which Rabbi Ḥanina taught:
If he wrote it with mei teriya or gallnut water,
it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes gallnut water and מי טריא, which are liquids but still make lasting writing, so a גט written with them is valid.

steps.title: רבי חייא adds lead, coal, and black paint
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches another ברייתא: a גט written with lead, coal, or black paint is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: if he wrote it with lead, with coal, or with black paint, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא with more materials that also count as lasting writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the list from the last step. Lead, coal, and black paint are not on the משנה's list of inks, but they leave a lasting mark, so they also fit 'anything that lasts.'
steps.whatToRemember: The test for writing a גט: does the writing last? Named inks, gallnut water, lead, coal, and black paint all pass. Liquids and juices that fade do not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
If he wrote it with lead, with coal, or with black paint,
it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to step 11 with a second ברייתא, next to רבי חנינא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written with lead, coal, or black paint is valid.

steps.title: Ink over red dye on שבת: two violations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both rule that someone who writes ink over red-dye letters on שבת is liable twice: once for writing and once for erasing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: someone who traces ink over red dye on שבת, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say he is liable for two: one for writing and one for erasing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching about inks, this time about the laws of שבת. It covers tracing one ink over another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When black ink goes over red letters, new ink letters appear, which is writing. At the same moment the red letters are covered up, which is erasing. So one act breaks two שבת prohibitions.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר: הַמַּעֲבִיר דְּיוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי סִיקְרָא, בַּשַּׁבָּת;
phrases.english: It was stated: One who passes ink over red dye on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish both say:
He is liable for two:
phrases.notes: He would have to bring two separate offerings, one for each violation.

phrases.english: one for writing,
and one for erasing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הַמַּעֲבִיר דְּיוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי סִיקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related topic: after discussing inks for a גט, the גמרא turns to inks in the laws of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tracing ink over red dye on שבת counts as both writing and erasing, so he is liable twice.

steps.title: Same over same is exempt; red over ink is disputed
steps.stepSummary: Tracing ink over ink, or red dye over red dye, is exempt. Tracing red dye over ink: some say he is liable and some say he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ink over ink, or red dye over red dye, he is exempt. Red dye over ink: some say he is liable, and some say he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the שבת teaching by covering the other combinations of inks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the same ink goes over the same ink, nothing changes on the page, so he is exempt. Red over black is the opposite of the case in step 14, and the text records two views on it without settling which is right.
steps.whatToRemember: Ink over red dye: liable twice. Same over same: exempt. Red dye over ink: left as a disagreement.

phrases.english: Ink on top of ink,
red dye on top of red dye: he is exempt.
Red dye on top of ink:
some say he is liable,
and some say he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the שבת teaching from step 14 by going through the other ink combinations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same ink over the same ink is exempt. For red dye over ink, there are two views: liable or exempt.

steps.title: Why some say liable and some say exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two opinions about tracing red dye over ink on שבת. One side calls it erasing. The other side calls it ruining, which is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he is liable, because it counts as erasing. Some say he is exempt, because he is only ruining something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each side of the dispute from the last step, about tracing red dye over ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side that says liable sees covering the ink as erasing it, since the good ink writing is now hidden. The side that says exempt sees it as ruining good writing by covering it with worse writing. Destructive acts like that are not punishable מלאכות on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Erasing, one of the מלאכות forbidden on שבת
Someone who ruins or acts destructively; he is exempt on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Ink over red dye counts as writing and erasing together. Red dye over ink is disputed: is it erasing, or just ruining?

phrases.english: Some say he is liable –
phrases.notes: This goes back to the last case: tracing red dye over letters already written in ink.

phrases.english: it is erasing.
Some say he is exempt –
he is ruining.
phrases.notes: He covered good ink writing with weaker red writing. That is damage, and damaging acts are not liable on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind each side of the dispute stated in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Red dye over ink is either erasing (liable) or ruining (exempt).

steps.title: Can witnesses trace over names written for them in red dye?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether witnesses who cannot write may sign a גט by tracing over their names, which were first written for them in red dye.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: If witnesses do not know how to sign, may someone write their names for them in red dye so that they sign on top of it? Does writing on top of other writing count as writing or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from שבת to the laws of a גט. ריש לקיש asks whether tracing over existing letters counts as the witnesses' own signature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question uses the same case as the שבת rules: ink over red dye. If the upper writing counts as writing, these witnesses could sign this way. If it does not count, their signature would not be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper writing: writing done on top of other writing

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Witnesses who do not know how to sign;
may someone write [their names] for them in red dye,
and they sign as upper writing?
phrases.notes: He means the witnesses trace over the red letters with ink.

phrases.english: Is it writing, or is it not writing?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'ink over red dye' case from the שבת rules and asks about it for signing a גט.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether upper writing (ink traced over red dye) counts as a valid signature for witnesses.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says it is not writing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that writing on top of other writing does not count as writing for the witnesses' signature.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not writing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's question: the witnesses may not sign this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a גט, tracing over letters that are already there is not real writing. So these witnesses have not truly signed.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Upper writing is not valid writing for the witnesses' signature.

steps.title: But you taught that upper writing counts for שבת
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן with his own teaching: upper writing counts as writing for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But didn't our teacher teach us that upper writing counts as writing for שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש points out that רבי יוחנן's answer seems to contradict what רבי יוחנן himself taught about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, ink over red dye on שבת makes a person liable for writing. So upper writing is real writing there. Why should it not count as writing for a גט?

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't our teacher teach us,
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is speaking to רבי יוחנן himself, politely calling him 'our teacher'.

phrases.english: upper writing is writing regarding שבת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18 using רבי יוחנן's own ruling from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that upper writing is not writing for a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If upper writing counts as writing for שבת, it should count as writing for a גט too.

steps.title: A comparison is not enough to act on
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that just because we compare the two areas of law, we may not actually rely on that comparison when making a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Just because we compare them, should we actually act on it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his ruling. Calling upper writing 'writing' for שבת does not mean we may use it in a real גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting upper writing as writing for שבת is one thing. Relying on it to make a גט valid is something more serious. A גט touches on whether a woman is truly divorced, so רבי יוחנן will not rely on the comparison there.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it really so that
Shall we act on it in practice

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rule in one area of הלכה cannot automatically be used to act in another area, especially when acting is serious, like with a גט.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָנוּ מְדַמִּין
phrases.english: He said to him: And just because we compare,
phrases.notes: He means comparing the laws of a גט to the laws of שבת.

phrases.english: shall we act on it in practice?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָנוּ מְדַמִּין נַעֲשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between making a comparison and relying on it in practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Upper writing counts as writing for שבת, so it should count for a גט too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A comparison made for שבת is not strong enough to rely on in practice for a גט.

steps.title: רב: a paper stencil filled in with ink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute about what to do for witnesses who cannot sign. רב says to cut their names out of blank paper and have the witnesses fill in the gaps with ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Witnesses who do not know how to sign — רב says: We cut out blank paper for them, and they fill in the cut-out spaces with ink.
steps.whatsHappening: Since tracing over red dye does not work, the גמרא gives רב's practical solution for witnesses who cannot write.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a stencil, the witnesses' ink goes straight onto the document, not on top of other writing. So it is real writing, not upper writing.

phrases.english: It was stated: Witnesses who do not know how to sign;

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: מְקָרְעִין לָהֶם נְיָיר חָלָק,
phrases.english: Rav says: We cut out blank paper for them,
phrases.notes: The letters of their names are cut out of the paper, like a stencil laid on the גט.

phrases.english: and they fill in the cut-out spaces with ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical method, now that tracing over red dye has been ruled out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who cannot sign may fill in a paper stencil of their names with ink.

steps.title: שמואל: write their names with lead
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a different method: write the witnesses' names with lead first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: With lead.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב and gives his own way to help witnesses who cannot sign: their names are first written with lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lead leaves a mark that the witnesses can follow when they sign. שמואל does not see this as the problem of upper writing that רבי יוחנן ruled out with red dye.

keyTerms.meaning: And שמואל says (the other side of the dispute)

steps.whatToRemember: Tracing over red dye is not valid writing for witnesses (רבי יוחנן). For witnesses who cannot sign, רב uses a paper stencil filled in with ink, and שמואל uses names written first in lead.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says: With lead.
phrases.notes: Their names are written with lead first, and the witnesses then write over those letters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב's method in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who cannot sign have their names written first with lead.

steps.title: How can lead be used if lead counts as real writing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's lead method from a ברייתא of רבי חייא that says a גט written with lead is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would you really think they write the names with lead? But רבי חייא taught: if he wrote it with lead, with coals, or with black paint, it is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's suggestion from step 22. If lead counts as real writing, then the witnesses' ink on top of it would be 'writing on top of writing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, רבי יוחנן said writing on top of other writing does not count as a signature. רבי חייא's ברייתא shows that lead is real writing, since a גט written with it is כשר. So the witnesses tracing over lead would not be signing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (an expression of surprise)

phrases.english: With lead — could that enter your mind?!
But didn't Rabbi Chiyya teach:
If he wrote it with lead,
with coals or with black paint – it is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּאֲבָר סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ?! וְהָתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's method from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's suggestion to pre-write the witnesses' names in lead.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lead is valid writing per רבי חייא, so ink over it is writing on top of writing, which רבי יוחנן said is not a signature.

steps.title: Plain lead versus lead-ink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל meant plain lead, which is not real writing, while רבי חייא meant ink made from lead water.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this case is with lead itself, and that case is with lead water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by splitting the two cases. Each source is talking about a different kind of lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rubbing with a piece of lead itself is not considered writing, so the witnesses can trace over it. Water blackened with lead is a real ink, and that is what רבי חייא said is valid for a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources talk about different cases
Lead water: water darkened with lead, used as ink

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one – with lead itself,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is שמואל's method, which uses a plain piece of lead.

phrases.english: that one – with lead water.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא – בַּאֲבָרָא, הָא – בְּמַיָּא דַאֲבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): two different materials.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any lead counts as writing, so שמואל's method fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain lead is not writing and can be traced over; only lead-ink is valid writing.

steps.title: רבי אבהו suggests gall water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו offers a third method: write the witnesses' names with gall water and let them trace over it in ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: with gall water.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives his own method for witnesses who cannot sign. Instead of lead, the names are first written with gall water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This joins the list started by רב and שמואל. The idea is the same: the first marking must not count as real writing, so the witnesses' ink becomes the true signature.

keyTerms.meaning: Gall water: water in which gallnuts were soaked

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: with gall water.
phrases.notes: He means the names are written first with gall water, and the witnesses then trace over them in ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another method alongside רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses' names may be pre-written with gall water for them to trace.

steps.title: But gall water is valid writing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו from רבי חנינא's teaching that a גט written with gallnut water is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חנינא taught: if he wrote it with מי טריא or gallnut water, it is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The same kind of challenge comes back. If gall water is real writing, tracing over it is again writing on top of writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא says a גט written with gallnut water is כשר, so gall water counts as writing. That would make the witnesses' ink on top of it worthless as a signature, just like the problem with lead.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of colored liquid used for writing

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chanina teach:
If he wrote it with mei teriya or gallnut water – it is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָנֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: כְּתָבוֹ בְּמֵי טַרְיָא וְאַפְצָא – כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's method from step 25.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gall water is valid writing for a גט, so tracing over it is writing on top of writing.

steps.title: It depends on whether the parchment was treated with gallnuts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אבהו speaks of parchment treated with gallnuts, where gall water does not last; רבי חנינא speaks of untreated parchment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is where the parchment was treated with gallnuts, and that is where it was not, because gall water does not hold on top of gall water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again splits the cases, this time by the type of parchment. On gall-treated parchment, gall water writing does not last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing that does not last is not real writing, so the witnesses can sign over it. On plain parchment, gall water does last, and that is why רבי חנינא calls it valid for a גט.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where it was processed with gallnuts, that is where it was not processed;
phrases.notes: 'It' is the parchment. רבי אבהו's case is treated parchment; רבי חנינא's case is untreated.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מֵי מֵילִין עַל גַּבֵּי מֵי מֵילִין.
phrases.english: for gall water does not hold on top of gall water.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דַּאֲפִיץ, הָא דְּלָא אֲפִיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): treated versus untreated parchment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gall water always counts as writing.
steps.terutzMaskana: On gall-treated parchment gall water does not last, so it is not writing and may be traced over.

steps.title: רב פפא suggests saliva, and used it in practice
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says to pre-write the names with saliva, and he actually ruled this way for a cattle herder named פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: with saliva. And so רב פפא instructed פפא the ox herder: with saliva.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth method is given: saliva. The גמרא adds that רב פפא really applied it for someone who could not sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saliva leaves no lasting mark at all, so it clearly is not writing, and no challenge is raised. The story shows this was a real practical ruling, not just theory.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: with saliva.
And so Rav Pappa instructed
Pappa the ox herder: with saliva.
phrases.notes: This פפא is a different person, a witness who did not know how to sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another method after רבי אבהו's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names may be pre-written with saliva for the witnesses to trace, as practiced by רב פפא.

steps.title: This help is only for a גט, not for money documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the whole leniency of tracing names to גיטין; for financial documents it is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to bills of divorce, but for documents – no,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on all the methods just listed. The next step backs up this limit with a story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Letting witnesses trace their names is a special allowance for a גט, so a woman is not left unable to remarry for lack of witnesses. For ordinary שטרות, one must find witnesses who can sign properly.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to (a limiting phrase)

steps.whatToRemember: Lead, gall water on treated parchment, and saliva all work because the first marking is not real writing; and this whole allowance is only for a גט.

phrases.english: And this applies only to bills of divorce,
but for documents – no,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּגִיטִּין, אֲבָל בִּשְׁטָרוֹת – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits all the tracing methods given so far to גיטין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tracing pre-written names is allowed for a גט but not for financial documents.

steps.title: רב כהנא punishes someone who used tracing for ordinary documents
steps.stepSummary: A man allowed witnesses to trace their names on regular financial documents, and רב כהנא had him flogged. This backs up the rule that tracing is allowed only for גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: For there was a certain man who acted this way with other documents, and רב כהנא had him flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to back up the rule from the last step: tracing names is not allowed for שאר שטרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 said the tracing leniency is only for a גט. This story shows the rule was enforced in practice. Someone used the method for ordinary documents, and רב כהנא punished him. So the line between גיטין and financial documents is a real, practical limit.

keyTerms.meaning: an actual deed or ruling in practice
other documents, meaning ordinary financial documents (not a גט)

steps.whatToRemember: Tracing over pre-written names is a special leniency only for גיטין. Using it for financial documents was treated seriously enough that רב כהנא had the person flogged.

phrases.english: For there was a certain man who acted this way
with other documents,
and רב כהנא had him flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 29's limit (only for גיטין) with a real case where breaking it was punished.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that tracing pre-written names is not allowed for financial documents.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case: רב כהנא had a man flogged for allowing tracing on ordinary documents.
